text:
With 1:18 left in Las Vegas, the Golden Knights led 3-2 and had seen this movie end the right way plenty of times. Adin Hill even tried to score into the empty Dallas net; the puck slipped off his stick and slid just wide, as Jesse Granger of The Athletic noted. A minute later Mikko Rantanen scored on a 1% chance with five seconds left, and in overtime Miro Heiskanen, back in the lineup after missing five straight games, finished it 4-3. Our win chance for Dallas had sat at 1% before Rantanen's goal.

For two periods and change this was a Vegas game. William Karlsson scored 40 seconds into the second, and when Trevor Connelly faked a shot and fed him for a one-timer at 10:27 of the third, it was 2-0. Connelly, the 2024 first-rounder, had two assists, six shots and an on-ice expected goals against of 0.08 in almost 17 minutes, which is as close to a perfect shift log as you see. Nils Lundkvist answered 32 seconds later, Jack Eichel's no-look backhand from behind the net set up Brett Howden for 3-1 (Brayden McNabb's assist was the 200th point of his career), and Vegas went up a period in chances, 1.37 expected goals to 0.88 in the third.

Then the Stars' best players took over. Wyatt Johnston buried a lucky deflection at 18:42, Rantanen tied it, and Heiskanen won it 3:36 into overtime, a goal worth 51% of a win on its own. Rantanen finished with a goal and three assists in 24 minutes. Jake Oettinger made the save of the night in overtime on Karlsson, a 16% look with nearly half a win riding on it.

Over 65 minutes the chances leaned Vegas, 3.22 expected goals (the quality of shots) to 2.80, and by our replays the Golden Knights deserved this one 52% of the time, which is to say it was a coin flip that Dallas stole late. The Stars have won three straight, and they did it in the same week Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points. Vegas went 0 for 5 on the power play, and that is the stat that will sting.
headline: Rantanen ties it with five seconds left, Heiskanen wins it
